\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB/CALCULUS BC 2014 SCORING GUIDELINES}

\section*{Question 3}

The function \(f\) is defined on the closed interval \([-5,4]\). The graph of \(f\) consists of three line segments and is shown in the figure above. Let \(g\) be the function defined by \(g(x)=\int_{-3}^{x} f(t) d t\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Find \(g(3)\).
\item[(b)] On what open intervals contained in \(-5<x<4\) is the graph of \(g\) both increasing and concave down? Give a reason for your answer.
\item[(c)] The function \(h\) is defined by \(h(x)=\frac{g(x)}{5 x}\). Find \(h^{\prime}(3)\).
\item[(d)] The function \(p\) is defined by \(p(x)=f\left(x^{2}-x\right)\). Find the slope of the line tangent to the graph of \(p\) at the point where \(x=-1\).
\item[(a)] \(g(3)=\int_{-3}^{3} f(t) d t=6+4-1=9\)
\item[(b)] \(g^{\prime}(x)=f(x)\)
The graph of \(g\) is increasing and concave down on the intervals \(-5<x<-3\) and \(0<x<2\) because \(g^{\prime}=f\) is positive and decreasing on these intervals.
\item[(c)] \(h^{\prime}(x)=\frac{5 x g^{\prime}(x)-g(x) 5}{(5 x)^{2}}=\frac{5 x g^{\prime}(x)-5 g(x)}{25 x^{2}}\)
\[
\begin{aligned}
h^{\prime}(3) & =\frac{(5)(3) g^{\prime}(3)-5 g(3)}{25 \cdot 3^{2}} \\
& =\frac{15(-2)-5(9)}{225}=\frac{-75}{225}=-\frac{1}{3}
\end{aligned}
\]
\item[(d)] \(p^{\prime}(x)=f^{\prime}\left(x^{2}-x\right)(2 x-1)\)
\[
p^{\prime}(-1)=f^{\prime}(2)(-3)=(-2)(-3)=6
\]
\end{itemize}
